MS Excel: Workbook
The file containing one or more worksheets.
Worksheet
One grid of rows and columns within a workbook.
Cell
The intersection of a row and a column.
Range
A group of referenced cells such as A1:C5.
Formula bar
The area that shows or edits the active cell's contents.
Name box
The box normally displaying the active cell's address.
Absolute reference
A reference such as $B$2 that stays fixed when a formula is copied.
Relative reference
A reference such as B2 that adjusts when a formula is copied.
Mixed reference
A reference with exactly one fixed part, such as $B2.
SUM
The function that adds numeric values.
AVERAGE
The function that calculates the arithmetic mean.
MIN
The function that returns the smallest number.
MAX
The function that returns the largest number.
COUNT
The function that counts cells containing numbers.
COUNTA
The function that counts nonempty cells, including ones containing text.
COUNTIF
The function that counts cells meeting one specified condition.
SUMIF
The function that adds values according to one specified condition.
IF
The function that chooses between two results using a logical test.
ROUND
The function that rounds a number to a specified number of digits.
LEN
The function that returns the character count of a text string.
LEFT
The function that extracts characters from the beginning of a string.
RIGHT
The function that extracts characters from the end of a string.
TODAY
The function that returns the current date without a time component.
NOW
The function that returns the current date and time.
Sort
The operation that rearranges rows into a chosen order.
Filter
The operation that displays only rows matching specified criteria.
Freeze Panes
The feature that keeps chosen rows or columns visible while scrolling.
Wrap Text
The feature that shows long cell content on multiple lines.
Conditional Formatting
Formatting that changes when a value meets a rule.
Data Validation
Rules that restrict the values a user can enter in a cell.
PivotTable
An interactive summary that groups and aggregates records.
Fill handle
The small selection corner used to copy values or extend a series.
Column chart
A chart comparing categories using vertical bars.
Line chart
A chart connecting points to show a trend.
Print area
The saved worksheet range selected for printing.
PowerPoint: The file that contains the slide deck.
A predefined arrangement of placeholders on a slide.
A layout box designed to receive content such as a title or picture.
A coordinated set of colours, fonts and effects.
The top-level design that controls common features of associated layouts.
The view showing a grid of slide thumbnails for reordering.
The area for writing a speaker's notes for a slide.
The speaker display with notes and slide controls.
The mode that presents the slides to the audience.
An effect displayed when moving between slides.
An effect applied to an object on a slide.
The list used to inspect and reorder object effects.
An animation that makes an object appear.
An animation that makes an object disappear.
An animation that moves an object along a specified route.
The amount of time an animation effect runs.
The wait before an animation begins.
The animation start setting that waits for a click.
The animation start setting that begins with the preceding effect.
The animation start setting that waits for the preceding effect to finish.
The command that keeps a slide in the file while skipping it in a normal show.
The command that creates a copy of a selected slide.
A named group used to organise related slides.
An independently placed container for text.
A diagram graphic for relationships, processes or hierarchies.
A graphic that plots numerical values from a data series.
A grid for organising text or values in cells.
The picture operation that trims outer image areas.
The command that lines up the left edges of selected objects.
The command that spaces selected objects evenly across a horizontal area.
The command that lets several selected objects be moved as one.
The command that places an object above other overlapping objects.
A clickable connection to a slide, file or webpage.
Printed audience pages that can contain several slide thumbnails.
MS Access: Table
The database object that stores records in rows and fields in columns.
Record
All the field values in one table row.
Field
One named category of data in a table.
Primary key
A field or field combination that uniquely identifies each record.
Foreign key
A field used to reference a key in a related table.
One-to-many relationship
A relationship in which one parent row can match several child rows.
Referential integrity
A rule preventing child references to nonexistent parent keys.
Select query
A database request that retrieves records without changing them.
Append query
An action query that adds records to an existing table.
Update query
An action query that changes field values in matching records.
Delete query
An action query that removes matching records.
Make-table query
A query that creates a new table from its results.
Parameter query
A query that asks for an input value when it runs.
Crosstab query
A query that summarises data using row and column headings.
Form
An interface for entering or viewing records using controls.
Report
A formatted output object for presenting or printing database information.
Datasheet View
The view that shows data as a grid of rows and columns.
Design View for a table
The view for specifying fields, data types and field properties.
Short Text
The field type suited to short names and alphanumeric codes.
Long Text
The field type intended for lengthy notes and descriptions.
Yes/No
The field type for a two-state value.
AutoNumber
The field type that automatically generates a value for each new record.
Currency
The numeric field type intended for monetary amounts with fixed precision.
Date/Time
The field type designed for calendar dates and times.
Attachment
The field type that can store files with a record in an ACCDB database.
Validation Rule
A field property specifying which values are acceptable.
Validation Text
The message shown when an entered value breaks a validation rule.
Default Value
The property that supplies an initial value for new records.
Required
The field property that prevents saving a Null value.
Input Mask
A pattern guiding how characters are entered into a field.
Index
A structure that helps locate and sort records by indexed fields.
Criteria
The condition that determines which rows a query includes.
Ascending sort
The order that places lower numbers before higher numbers.
Combo box
A form control that offers values in a drop-down list.
Subform
A form embedded in another form to display related records.
Tally Prime: Company
The accounting data set maintained for one business entity.
Ledger
An account in which transactions for one party, asset or category are recorded.
Group
A classification that gathers ledgers of a similar nature.
Voucher
A record used to enter a business transaction.
Receipt voucher
The voucher normally used for money received from a customer.
Payment voucher
The voucher normally used for paying an expense from cash or bank.
Contra voucher
The voucher for internal transfers between cash and bank accounts.
Journal voucher
The voucher typically used for a non-cash accounting adjustment.
Sales voucher
The voucher used to record a sale to a customer.
Purchase voucher
The voucher used to record a supplier purchase.
Credit note for sales return
The document reducing a customer's balance for goods they returned.
Debit note for purchase return
The document recording a reduction in the amount owed for goods returned to a supplier.
Sales order
The order received from a customer before supply.
Purchase order
The order issued to a supplier before receiving goods.
Delivery note
The inventory document recording goods sent out for delivery.
Receipt note
The inventory document recording goods received from a supplier.
Stock item
A distinct product whose quantities are tracked.
Stock group
A classification used to organise similar stock items.
Unit of measure
The quantity basis for an item, such as kilograms or pieces.
Godown
A storage location used to track where goods are kept.
Stock Journal
The inventory voucher used to transfer stock between locations.
Physical Stock voucher
The voucher used to enter an actual counted stock quantity.
Batch number
An identifier shared by units from the same production lot.
Opening balance
The amount carried into an account at the start of the period.
Closing balance
The account balance at the end of the reporting period.
Trial Balance
The report used to compare total debit and credit balances.
Balance Sheet
The statement showing assets, liabilities and equity on a date.
Profit and Loss Account
The statement showing income, expenses and the period's profit or loss.
Day Book
The report listing transactions recorded for a chosen date or period.
Stock Summary
The report summarising quantities and values of inventory.
Bills receivable
Outstanding amounts customers owe the business.
Bills payable
Outstanding amounts the business owes its suppliers.
Cost centre
An accounting unit used to allocate and analyse costs or income.
Bank reconciliation
The process of matching book entries with the bank statement.
Backup
A separate recoverable copy of company data.
Marg ERP: The saved product record reused when creating bills.
The party from whom the business purchases goods.
The party to whom the business sells goods.
The request sent to a supplier specifying goods and quantities wanted.
The customer's order for goods before fulfilment.
The transaction documenting a purchase from a supplier.
The bill issued to a customer for a sale.
The transaction recording goods sent back to a supplier.
The transaction recording goods a customer sends back.
The identifier that groups stock from one manufacturing lot.
The date used to identify when a stock batch expires.
The date on which a product batch was made.
A machine-readable code scanned to identify an item.
The marked maximum retail price on a packaged product.
The unit price at which the business buys an item.
The unit price charged to a customer before any applicable adjustments.
A reduction from a quoted price.
The number of units on a bill line.
The basis for counting an item, such as a box or a piece.
The quantity carried into inventory at the start of a period.
The quantity remaining at the end of a period.
The stock threshold used to signal replenishment.
Movement of goods between storage locations within the business.
The quantity found by counting the goods actually on hand.
A difference between the recorded quantity and the physical count.
The record of transactions affecting a particular account.
An unpaid amount due from a customer.
An unpaid amount owed to a supplier.
The date by which an outstanding bill is to be paid.
A sale for which the customer will pay later.
A sale settled by a cash payment at the time of sale.
An entry recording money paid out.
The process of assigning a monetary value to inventory on hand.
A recoverable copy of business data.
Photoshop: Layer
An independently editable level in an image's stack.
Layer mask
A grayscale control that hides or reveals portions of a layer.
Adjustment layer
A layer that applies a tonal or colour correction non-destructively.
Opacity
The setting controlling how transparent the entire layer appears.
Blend mode
The rule governing how a layer combines with layers below it.
Smart Object
A container that preserves source content through repeated transforms.
Smart Filter
An editable filter applied to a Smart Object.
Layer group
A folder used to organise layers.
Move tool
The tool for repositioning selected layer content.
Rectangular Marquee
The tool for making a rectangular selection.
Elliptical Marquee
The tool for making an oval selection.
Lasso tool
The tool for drawing a freehand selection boundary.
Polygonal Lasso
The tool for making a selection from straight line segments.
Magic Wand
The tool for selecting areas based on similar colour values.
Crop tool
The tool used to trim the outer boundaries of an image.
Eyedropper
The tool for sampling a colour from the image.
Brush tool
The tool for painting strokes using a brush tip.
Clone Stamp
The tool for copying pixels from a sampled source area.
Healing Brush
The tool that blends sampled texture with the destination's surrounding tone.
Type tool
The tool for adding editable text.
Pen tool
The tool for drawing precise paths with anchor points.
Gradient tool
The tool that creates a gradual transition between colours.
Hand tool
The tool for panning the document view.
Zoom tool
The tool for changing on-screen magnification.
Histogram
A graph of the distribution of tonal values in an image.
Levels
The adjustment for setting the black point, midtones and white point using sliders.
Curves
The adjustment that changes tone by shaping a curve on a graph.
Hue/Saturation
The adjustment used to alter hue and colour intensity.
Grayscale
The image mode that represents tones without colour.
RGB
The colour model based on red, green and blue light.
CMYK
The colour model based on cyan, magenta, yellow and black inks.
PSD
The native Photoshop document format commonly used to retain layers.
JPEG
The commonly used photographic format with lossy compression and no alpha transparency.
PNG
The lossless raster format commonly used for web graphics with transparency.
Feather
The selection setting that softens the transition at its edge.
InPage: Text box
A frame that holds editable text in a page layout.
Picture box
A frame intended to hold a placed image.
Page margin
The space between the page edge and the main content area.
Gutter between columns
The blank space separating adjacent text columns.
Column
One of the vertical text areas into which a page is divided.
Portrait orientation
A page that is taller than it is wide.
Landscape orientation
A page that is wider than it is tall.
Page size
The physical width and height chosen for the page.
Right-to-left direction
The base writing direction normally used for Urdu text.
Left-to-right direction
The base writing direction normally used for English text.
Typeface
The visual design of a family of letters or characters.
Point size
The typographic measurement controlling the nominal size of text.
Bold
A heavier text weight used for emphasis.
Italic
A slanted type style used for emphasis.
Underline
A line placed beneath text for emphasis.
Baseline
The reference line on which most letters sit.
Line spacing
The vertical distance between successive lines of text.
Paragraph spacing
Extra vertical space placed before or after a paragraph.
First-line indent
An inset applied only to the first line of a paragraph.
Hanging indent
An arrangement in which later lines are indented farther than the first line.
Left alignment
Text arranged with a flush left edge and a ragged right edge.
Right alignment
Text arranged with a flush right edge and a ragged left edge.
Centre alignment
Text positioned centrally between the left and right boundaries.
Justification
Paragraph alignment that adjusts spacing to line up both sides on full lines.
Header
Content positioned in the top area of a page.
Footer
Content positioned in the bottom area of a page.
Page number
A label identifying a page's position in the document.
Caption
A short description placed with an illustration or photograph.
Body text
The main continuous reading text of a publication.
Headline
The prominent title introducing an article.
Bullet list
A list in which items are introduced by symbols rather than running numbers.
Numbered list
A list in which items are marked in an ordered sequence.
Aspect ratio
The relationship between an image's width and height.
Proofreading
Checking the laid-out text for spelling and typographic mistakes.
Print preview
A view used to inspect the page layout before printing.
Outlook: Inbox
The folder that normally receives incoming mail.
Drafts
The folder for saved messages that have not yet been sent.
Sent Items
The folder containing copies of messages already sent.
Outbox
The folder for messages waiting to be sent.
Deleted Items
The folder that normally receives messages when they are first deleted.
Junk Email
The folder for messages classified as suspected spam.
To
The field for the primary recipients of a message.
Cc
The field for visible recipients receiving a copy.
Bcc
The field for recipients whose addresses are hidden from other recipients.
Subject
The short heading that identifies a message's topic.
Attachment
A file included with an email message.
Reply
The command that addresses a response to the original sender.
Reply All
The command that responds to the sender and other visible original recipients.
Forward
The command that sends a received message on to other recipients.
Signature
A reusable closing block added to outgoing messages.
Automatic Replies
The feature that responds to incoming mail while a user is away.
Rule
A set of conditions and actions for automatically handling messages.
Category
A label that organises related messages or calendar items.
Follow-up flag
A marker that indicates a message needs later action.
Mark as unread
The command that restores an item's unread status.
Archive
The action that moves a message out of the Inbox to an archive folder.
Search
The feature used to locate messages matching words or criteria.
Conversation view
An arrangement that groups related messages into a thread.
Calendar
The area for scheduling appointments and meetings.
Appointment
A calendar entry for the user's own schedule without invited attendees.
Meeting request
An invitation asking attendees to join a scheduled event.
Recurring event
A calendar event that repeats according to a pattern.
Reminder
A notification set to occur before a scheduled item.
All-day event
A calendar entry that occupies a date without specific start and end times.
Scheduling Assistant
The tool that compares attendees' availability for a meeting.
Location field
The meeting field identifying where an event takes place.
Accept
The meeting response indicating that the invitee plans to attend.
Tentative
The meeting response indicating possible attendance.
Decline
The meeting response indicating the invitee will not attend.
Contact
A saved person record containing addresses or other contact details.
